name: Pro Micro (ATmega32U4)
summary: ATmega32U4 with native USB, so it can be a keyboard or a mouse without a helper chip. The board in most custom keyboard builds. USB at the top.
logic: 5 V at 16 MHz, or 3.3 V at 8 MHz
notes: Native USB is the whole point. The 32U4 does USB itself, so the board can enumerate as a keyboard, mouse or MIDI device. That is why QMK and every handwired keyboard uses it.

There are two serial ports and they are not the same thing. Serial is the USB connection to your computer; Serial1 is the hardware UART on pins 0 and 1. Code written for a Uno that expects Serial on the TX and RX pins will not work.

The bootloader only listens for under a second after a single reset, or about eight seconds after a quick double reset. Upload a sketch that hangs or kills USB and the board stops enumerating. The recovery is to short RST to GND twice quickly and start the upload inside that window. This is the most common way a Pro Micro appears bricked.

There is a 5 V 16 MHz version and a 3.3 V 8 MHz version, and they look identical. Picking the wrong one in the IDE builds the sketch for the wrong clock speed. It uploads fine, then USB timing is off and the board no longer enumerates.

RAW is the unregulated input, up to 12 V, feeding the on-board regulator. VCC is the regulated rail, and it is an output when the board is powered from RAW or USB. Feeding VCC directly bypasses the regulator.
The analog pins are not where a Uno user expects. There is no A4 or A5. The ADC lives on A0 to A3 (pins 18 to 21) and A6 to A10 (pins 4, 6, 8, 9, 10).
I2C is on pins 2 and 3, not on the analog pins.
The micro-USB connector on the cheap clones is held on by solder pads alone and tears off. Glue it, or buy a USB-C clone.

pins.name: TXO
pins.note: Hardware UART, not the USB serial. Use Serial1 in code.

pins.name: D2
pins.note: I2C is here, not on the analog pins like a Uno.

pins.name: RAW
pins.note: Feeds the on-board regulator. About 4.8 V when running from USB.

pins.name: RST
pins.note: Short to GND twice quickly to force the bootloader. This is how you recover a board that stopped enumerating.

pins.name: VCC
pins.note: An output when powered from RAW or USB. Driving it directly bypasses the regulator.
